Geertgen tot Sint Jans - Holy Kinship ( c. 1485-1495)
What's going on on the altar? Is that a Saracen executing a Christian pilgrim while everyone in the foreground gossips and carries on with business as usual?

At the altar is a sculpture depicting Abraham's sacrifice of Isaac. Behind that sculpture, the altar is carved with scenes depicting Adam and Eve's expulsion from paradise. So with the woodcarvings, we have man's "fall from grace", and with Abraham's test, we have the lineage that will lead to Jesus, savior of mankind.

The Holy Kinship was a popular subject of art in Germany and the surrounding areas at the time. There was a tradition that Saint Anne (mother of BV Mary, and grandmother of Jesus) was married three times, and these paintings showed the lineage. There's even a little Latin poem that goes with it. Here is the translation:

Anna is usually said to have conceived three Marys,

Whom her husbands Joachim, Cleophas, and Salome begot.

These [Marys] the men Joseph, Alpheus, and Zebedee took in marriage.

The first bore Christ; the second bore James the Less,

Joseph the Just, with Simon [and] Jude;

The third, James the Greater and the winged John

So that explains all of the figures in the painting. The bottom right-hand corner shows St Elizabeth with the baby St John the Baptist in her lap. The other two Marys are behind her. The Blessed Virgin is in blue of course (although I'm not sure why her head is uncovered in this painting), holding baby Jesus. St Anne herself is shown seated with a book, her customary symbol. Her husband St Joachim is behind her with the white beard. St Joseph is next to him, holding a white Lily, his customary symbol. The disciples Simon, James, and John are shown as the youths in the middle of the painting, pouring wine into the chalice. Saint Jude Thaddeus (not Judas) is lighting the altar candles. Far from "people gossiping", this is a painting showing Saints and many martyrs all together in a type of family scene.
